notesStmt.note: This manuscript dates to sometime between March 1890, the latest postmark on the reverse, and December 1890, when Whitman sent this and other poems to Scribner's (see loc.00230).

After attempting and failing to publish "Death Dogs My Steps" in a periodical, Whitman combined it with several other short poems as "L. of G.'s Purport," which he included in Good-Bye My Fancy (1891).

lg.head: Death dogs my steps.
lg.l: I sing of life, yet mind me well of death;

To-day Death dogs my steps, and has for years,
my seated shape
Draws sometimes close ‸to me as face to face.
